title.narrative: Provision of emergency multi sectoral purpose Cash assistance to families affected by settler violence mass incidents

description.narrative: ltpgtSince October 2023, the situation in the West Bank has deteriorated significantly with a huge increase in violence which has seen 1,005 Palestinians killed and over 9,500 injured by Israeli security forces and settlers, and heightened movement restrictions which limit access to essential services. Settler violence in particular has surged in the past 20 months, against Palestinian communities in Area C and, increasingly in Area B. The most common attacks include physical assault, intimidation, arson and stone-throwing. Over 740 settler attacks occurred in the first half of 2025, affecting 200 Palestinian communities across the West Bank and injuring 340 Palestinians. The month of June saw the highest number of Palestinians injured by Israeli settlers (100) for the past 2 decades[1]. At the same time, since October 2023, the West Bank has faced a deepening economic crisis, as movement restrictions and denial of access to the Israeli labour market have significantly increased unemployment. ltbrgtThis project has been designed to address the gaps that might occur during the implementation of the emergency response programming within the framework of the West Bank Protection Consortium (WBPC) Project addressing settler violence incidents across the West Bank. With this fund secured under the 48-hour allocation, PUI will deploy an amount of 300,000 USD for the temporary displaced families due to mass incident of settler violence with a provision of 4,000 USD (average) for conditional cash support for urgent repairs. In addition, PUI will distribute emergency NFIs including kitchen and Bedding sets with a cost of 200 USD for families hosting the temporarily displaced families. ltbrgtThis project will contribute to the Shelter Cluster objective in the second track which is: “To provide emergency shelter solutions and essential non-food items—including shelter kits, rental support, and dignity items—for displaced families, with a focus on displacement hotspots such as refugee camps and communities in Area C affected by demolitions or violent evictions, incorporating protection-sensitive approaches and support for community hosting arrangements”. The scope of the conditional cash provision will be tailored to the specific needs of each family, with an average of 4000 USD per household. The interventions will be carried out using a mixed approach of cash and material supplies, when appropriate and feasible. ltbrgtlt/pgt
